models.observations: Iron's long reed-roof hall and two freestanding shield racks frame a wide central door. The turquoise ridge shield repeats the scale motif and survives reduction. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.
The outboard spear tips, colored shield bosses and ridge scale remain clear with plaster, slate and terracotta roof rows. The center passage is free. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

The glass roof over the stockade-like shield racks keeps the armory distinct in both future rows. The brass bosses stop the dark shields merging with the door. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.
The low steel roof, brick or concrete walls, and opposed shield racks create a legible mechanized armory. The small yard jar leaves the doorway open. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.
The hearth's warm arch, horned anvil and timber stump read distinctly in the early rows, with the cooling vessel by the workshop. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.
The fieldstone furnace is clearly separate from the tiled-roof smithy, and the light anvil horn contrasts with its stump through three age rows. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

The pale furnace, bright firemouth and glass-roof shelter remain distinct in the futuristic smithy. The cooling jar and hammer sit inside the working yard. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.
The independent flue, lit forge and raised anvil give a clear skyline beside the brick or Modern workshop. The arc of the entrance remains visible. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

The pale rooftop insulators, linking conductor and blue glazing establish the plant's electrical function across Modern, Information and Ascension. The entry and side sun insignia stay distinct. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

Three northlight ridges, glazed cap and high stack identify a production hall. The landing, goods crates and door make sense together in both future ages. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

The dark sawtooth roof and red or pale warehouse walls retain their strong thumbnail silhouette. Three loading stairs serve the accessible central door. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.
The twin high flues and connecting pipe distinguish the advanced foundry. Its bright ladle rim is visibly truncated beside the wall. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.
defects: Move the ladle and its trunnions forward or create an open recess. The rim currently reaches z=-0.219 while the hall front is z=-0.345, clipping about 0.126 of the bowl and its molten contents into the wall.

The pale refractory shell and illuminated opening contrast with the glazed service shed. The ingots and cooling jar remain clear of the working mouth. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.
The bright fire mouth stays prominent in front of the red-brick chimney in Industrial and Modern. The two ingot molds sit separately by the small shed. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

The early timber loom and dye spools are recognizable full-size. At 64 px the striped panel covers virtually the entire doorway and its upper warp merges with the eaves. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

models.observations: The flywheel, glazing table and two colors of pots create an identifiable potter's yard. The roof changes among the middle ages while the door remains visible above the work bench. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

The low steel-roof shed and chimney serve a potter's wheel and loading bench. Glazed and unglazed vessels remain distinct against the working surfaces in both ages. The serialized GLB passes all three LOD checks.

The complete ladle, its two trunnions and axle now sit in front of the future foundry. The bright molten surface has an uninterrupted rim in both ages. Serialized validation passed for all three LODs.

The cast-metal ladle clears the factory facade beneath both the Industrial and Modern chimneys. The working supports remain on the pad and the loading door is visible. Serialized validation passed for all three LODs.

The narrowed early loom sits to one side of the doorway, with visible ivory warp above the woven stripes. The red spools leave a direct approach in Bronze and Iron. Serialized validation passed for all three LODs.
